tasks.title: Reduce Conversation History & Message Cloning
tasks.description: Heavy use of .clone() on full conversation_history, messages vectors, and individual Message objects in interactive.rs, acp/mod.rs, routers, and chat paths. This happens on every user turn. Switch to Arc<str> for content, bounded windows, or reference passing where possible.
tasks.details: All subtasks complete. ConversationItem.content switched to Arc<str> for cheap clones (interactive.rs). History building now uses direct slices + Arc clones instead of expensive rev/collect. System messages kept as single owned value. In ACP: brief write lock to extract data, then full tool/LLM loop with no lock held (local copies of messages/bayes). Many .clone() sites on history eliminated or made cheap. Fork still clones (required for semantics). Audit complete. Major per-turn clone reduction in interactive + ACP paths.

tasks.title: Make Interactive Suggestions Static / Lazy
tasks.description: In run_interactive_loop, a 25+ item Suggestion vector is rebuilt on every single user input (even before the user types). This is inside the per-turn loop and also wrapped in spawn_blocking. Move to a static or OnceLock.
tasks.details: All subtasks complete. Replaced the 26-item vec! (with owned Strings) inside every run_interactive_loop iteration with a std::sync::LazyLock<Vec<Suggestion>> using &'static str. Suggestion struct updated to &'static str fields. The spawn_blocking now only moves a cheap slice reference. Filtering still works. Dynamic model/cwd info stays only in the prompt (not in suggestions). Major reduction in per-keystroke allocations in interactive mode.

tasks.title: Establish Performance Baselines and Profiling Workflow
tasks.description: Before doing optimization work, capture current performance numbers so we can prove improvements. This includes wall time, allocations, and CPU profiles for key scenarios.
tasks.details:
**Goal**: Before making changes, capture repeatable "before" numbers for the key scenarios. This gives us objective proof when we later claim "Task 263 reduced allocations by X%".

Depends on the harness from task 266.

**Scenarios to baseline**:
1. Cold interactive start + first message (no tools)
2. 10-turn interactive chat with mixed tool use
3. ACP stdio session: startup + 5 tool-using turns
4. One-shot `grok chat "..."` 
5. Micro: tool registry lookup, prompt build, router.route()

**Tools**:
- hyperfine
- `cargo build --release --timings`
- flamegraph
- The new `--timing` mode
- Optional: dhat for allocations

**Output**: Store numbers in `Doc/PERF_BASELINES.md` (or similar) with date, commit, machine info, and raw output.

Update this task as we get numbers from the harness.
tasks.testStrategy: Documented baselines exist. Running the measurement harness produces repeatable numbers. All future perf PRs reference before/after.

tasks.title: Optimize Tool Execution Path (Arbitration + Dispatch)
tasks.description: Even after caching definitions, every tool call still goes through arbitration + a large match + argument extraction. Make this path as cheap as possible.
tasks.details:
**Context**: After task 263 (static tool defs), every tool call still pays:
- `tool_arbitration::arbitrate_tool_call(name, args)`
- Large `match name.as_str() { ... }` in `execute_tool`
- `require_str` / `require_*` helpers (small but per-call)
- Argument validation and context creation

**Goals**:
- Make the common path (read_file, list_directory, replace, web_search, etc.) as cheap as possible.
- Consider a faster dispatch mechanism once names are known to be static.
- Pre-compute required parameters map.

This is a follow-up optimization after the biggest wins.

tasks.title: Cargo / Build System & Binary Size Optimizations
tasks.description: The release profile is already quite good, but we can squeeze more (especially for distribution and cold starts). Also look at compile times.
tasks.details:
**Context**: The release profile is already reasonably aggressive (`lto = true`, `codegen-units=1`, `panic=abort`, `strip=true`).

There is still room for:
- Better binary size (important for distribution)
- Faster cold starts
- Potentially faster compile times for contributors
- Feature gating of heavy optional crates

This is lower priority than per-turn runtime wins but good for the overall project.
